title: India Raises Fuel Prices by Rs 3 Per Litre, Ending Four-Year Freeze

body:
India's state-run oil marketing companies on Thursday raised petrol and diesel prices by up to Rs 3 per litre nationwide, ending a four-year freeze that had been politically maintained through two rounds of state elections. Petrol in Delhi now costs Rs 97.77 per litre while diesel stands at Rs 90.67. Mumbai, Kolkata, and Chennai saw similar or steeper increases.

The hike, long anticipated by markets, was triggered by mounting under-recoveries at Indian Oil Corporation, Bharat Petroleum, and Hindustan Petroleum. The three companies have been absorbing losses estimated at Rs 1,000 crore per day as Brent crude holds above $104 per barrel, driven by the West Asia crisis and disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

The government attempted to soften the blow by simultaneously cutting additional excise duty on both fuels by Rs 10 per litre, though analysts at Livemint note the net impact on consumers remains a clear increase. RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra had warned last week that further hikes may be necessary if Middle East tensions persist.

For the Indian diaspora, the ripple effects are real. Higher diesel prices feed directly into transport and logistics costs, pushing up prices of everything from groceries to construction materials — a concern for NRIs funding family expenses or property projects back home. Inflation, which had begun moderating in early 2026, is expected to accelerate again in May and June.

Industry watchers say this is only the first tranche. State refiners reportedly plan a further Rs 2-5 per litre increase within weeks to close the gap between international crude costs and domestic pump prices. The political calculus — hiking after state polls but before monsoon season — is vintage New Delhi.
author: Diaspora Desk
